articles.title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history
articles.dek: It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again In many ways, there are striking parallels between the…
articles.description: It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years. Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed. Continue reading...

articles.dek: Cryptocurrency casino made Eva Elfie a brand ambassador Club end deal early citing ‘differing commercial priorities’ Leicester City have ditched their front-of-shirt…
articles.description: Cryptocurrency casino made Eva Elfie a brand ambassador Club end deal early citing ‘differing commercial priorities’ Leicester City have ditched their front-of-shirt sponsor, BC Game, after the cryptocurrency casino’s partnership with a porn actor sparked a fan backlash. BC Game, an offshore company registered in Belize that is unlicensed to operate in the UK , had been Leicester’s main sponsor since 2024. This month BC Game named Eva Elfie a brand ambassador, leading the Foxes Trust, Leicester’s supporters’ trust, to highlight the “devastating impacts” caused by gambling and pornography. On Wednesday the club said they prematurely ended their agreement with the online betting firm after they “recognised our differing commercial priorities”. Continue reading...

articles.description: The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history. Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville. Continue reading...

articles.description: Win over El Salvador would qualify US for Brazil 2027 Naomi Girma misses squad due to injury Sam Coffey returns after injury absence In the two years since the Paris Olympics, Emma Hayes has thoroughly tested fresh faces and new combinations, gathering a considerable amount of data about the US women’s national team. It’s been a thorough process, with 33 players earning their first caps since Hayes assumed the post, to bring her roster of options to 61 players. At last, the main event is nearing. On 27 November, the United States will enter the Concacaf W Championship with a clear objective: beat El Salvador. Winning the whole thing is nice, of course, and the USWNT have done so in nine of the tournament’s 11 installments to date. But by far the most important game on that journey is the first one, that quarter-final date with clear stakes: overcome El Salvador, or rely on a playoff to reach next summer’s World Cup. articles.dek: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry…
articles.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...
